analyst: Manual analysis using Claude Opus 5.5 for verification and code analysis

servers.server_cost: No separate price; early access only, "available on all Recurly subscription plans at general release"
servers.linked_cost: Starter $249/month + 0.9% of billing volume (first $40K per month free); All-Access from <1% (minimum $1M volume); Engage from $1,600/month; RevRec from $850/month
servers.pricing: Monthly fee + percentage of billing volume
servers.restrictions: Recurly site with the MCP feature flag enabled and rights on the site; tokens expire after 30 days; early access only
servers.governance_logic: The server is a facade for the vendor's own AI agents (Knowledge Agent, Coding Agent) - "exposes Recurly's agents to compatible AI tools". Site-level feature flag controls early access. The Cursor example lists both tools in autoApprove (no confirmation).
servers.structure_note: Thin MCP facade over internal vendor AI agents (each tool = one agent)
servers.agent_cannot: Any operations with account data: subscribers, subscriptions, invoices, payments, plans, reports (neither reading nor writing documented).
servers.docs_recs: None; the autoApprove example effectively recommends turning off confirmation.
servers.gov_promises: Not described; sign-in requires a Recurly account with site rights although the tools only work with documentation.
servers.notes: Endpoint https://mcp.recurly.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP). Tool descriptions quoted in the documentation.

Tools.desc: 2 tools, each an interface to a Recurly agent: docs_search (Knowledge Agent), api_reference_search (Coding Agent)
Tools.pre: docs_search: "Searches Recurly's documentation knowledge base to answer questions and surface relevant content"; api_reference_search: "Provides code examples, parameter references, library guidance, and explanations to help you get code running faster" (quoted in the docs; match with tools/list not verifiable)

Authorization.desc: OAuth (Recurly sign-in); protected resource metadata published; scope mcp:tools; tokens expire after 30 days

actions.desc: API reference, code examples and library guidance (Coding Agent)

observations.text: "An agent behind the tool": MCP is a thin wrapper around the vendor's internal AI agents (like Braze's Operator); the external AI talks to the internal one.
Authorization broader than necessary: reading public documentation requires sign-in to an account with site rights - possibly groundwork for future data tools.
Early access via a feature flag - the vendor opens the feature gradually.
